Subject: Recap & follow-up: data residency, retention, and failover (Pioneer Health)

Hi Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can properly scope the pilot and SOW: 

1) What we heard you care about today
- Patient PII never leaving the US and strict controls for logs/diagnostics
- Ability to pin inference to a US region (primary) with a documented cross-region failover plan
- Clear retention windows for user data + system logs and the option to reduce/disable retention for PHI
- Encrypted backups and proof points for RTO/RPO targets

2) Proposed next steps
- Marcus to answer the technical questions around retention, logging controls, and backup behavior (see Marcus in cc) — target EOD tomorrow for a concise A/B list
- We will attach SOC2 and our backup policy summary for your security team to review (attached)
- Camila to send a draft SOW and an estimated timeline for a US-only pilot (I’ll include standard runbook for failover behavior)

If I missed anything or priorities shifted, tell me and I’ll adjust. Can we tentatively target a technical follow-up on Wednesday 16th?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Recap & follow-up: data residency, retention, and failover (Pioneer Health)

Thanks Camila — appreciate the recap. A few clarifying questions from our security and infra leads before we open the SOW: 

- PII scope: can you confirm whether any model telemetry or cached KV state might contain patient identifiers by default? If so, how is that isolated?
- Retention: what are the configurable retention windows for (a) raw request logs, (b) aggregated metrics, (c) model KV cache? We may need 0-day retention for raw request logs for some workloads.
- Logging controls: is there selective sampling, redaction hooks, or a way to disable logging for specific endpoints?
- Region pinning / failover: can we pin to us-east-1 only and, in a catastrophic outage, failover to a secondary us-west region? What’s the expected RTO/RPO in that scenario and are backups cross-region by default?
- Encryption & key control: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?

If you can send a short, point-by-point reply we’ll share with our security team. Also please include any links to architecture diagrams or runbooks.

Alex
Alex Thompson
Director of Infrastructure, Pioneer Health
alex.thompson@pioneerhealth.com

--
P.S. We’ll need SOC2 and a sample network diagram for procurement to move the contract forward.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@pioneerhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & follow-up: data residency, retention, and failover (Pioneer Health)

Hi Alex — Marcus here (solutions engineering). Answering your questions succinctly: 

- PII scope
  - By default Redwood does not store PII in model weights or persistent caches. The KV cache used for decoding can include tokens from requests; it is treated as ephemeral and stored encrypted in-memory on the serving host. We offer a configuration to flush KV caches immediately after request completion for regulatory workloads.

- Retention (configurable per-customer)
  - Raw request logs: default 30 days; configurable down to 0 days (immediate deletion) for sensitive customers.
  - Aggregated metrics: default 90 days, can be reduced to 30 days; aggregated metrics are irreversibly anonymized and stored separately from request bodies.
  - Model KV cache: ephemeral by default; option to persist for short-term reuse (TTL) — default TTL is 1 hour, configurable to 0.

- Logging controls
  - We support: selective endpoint logging toggles, request redaction hooks (your parsers can strip or hash fields client-side), and a policy to disable request-body logging entirely for a route. Sampling is configurable (0–100%).

- Region pinning & failover
  - Yes — we support region pinning to a single primary region (e.g., us-east-1). Cross-region failover is supported as an automated policy: on sustained loss of capacity or zone-level outage we failover to your configured secondary region. Failover behavior: 
    - Traffic routing switch (< 60s for control-plane detection) 
    - Cold-start RTO depends on model size and pre-warmed capacity; for standard LLMs we target RTO <= 10 minutes if you reserve warm spare capacity; without warm spares, RTO can be 30–45 minutes.
    - RPO: with cross-region synchronous replication for customer metadata we can guarantee near-zero RPO for metadata; for runtime cache (KV) there is expected loss — we recommend treating KV as ephemeral and design for eventual consistency.
  - Backups: persistent artifacts (e.g., custom fine-tunes, customer config, audit logs) are backed up cross-region nightly by default and encrypted at rest. Backups are replicated to the DR region within 4 hours of snapshot completion.

- Encryption & keys
  - We support customer-managed keys via external KMS integration for stored data and backups. Network egress and control-plane interactions can be limited to private VPC endpoints in our Private deployment option.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Report_Q1_2026.pdf, prod-backup-policy-summary.pdf, pioneer-network-diagram.png. Sharing a concise runbook link below.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute tech session if you want us to walk through the failure mode timelines and options for warm spares.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus — that helps a lot. Two follow-ups for our procurement and security reviewers: 

1) Can you confirm the default retention values in writing (we need them in the SOW)?
2) For the cross-region backup SLA — is the 4-hour replication window in the standard private/dedicated offering or only for enterprise/private customers?

Also please add our security contact (security@pioneerhealth.com) to the next thread when you send the SOC2 and diagrams. If you can send a short SOW with options: (A) warm-spare-reserved pilot (faster RTO) and (B) cost-optimized pilot (no warm spares), we can route to procurement.

Alex
